hook: Step onto Mars without a suit. Your blood won't boil. Your spit will.
twist: Mars' air is under 1% of Earth's pressure, low enough for water to boil at body temperature, but your skin and blood vessels keep your blood under pressure; NASA's 1965 chamber accident subject stayed conscious about 14 seconds and remembered the water on his tongue beginning to boil.
angle: What would really happen to a human body on Mars without a suit, and which film myths are wrong?
risks: Body topic: kept to physics (pressure, boiling point), no gore; the bible keeps the channel out of body topics like food and sleep, and this is an environment question.
The 1965 test subject is a real person: he is not named or drawn; only NASA's account is used.
No scare claims: NASA's own statement that about half a minute is unlikely to cause permanent injury is labelled as NASA's estimate.
